free_tier.stated: 8 GiB of disk per PPA - current official reference: 'Disk space | 8 GiB; larger quotas considered on request at https://answers.launchpad.net/launchpad'. (Historical: PPAs were raised to a 2 GiB minimum in 2010 per the Launchpad blog; the 8 GiB figure is the current documented one.) 'PPAs per owner: One or more per user or team; each has its own URL.'
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: This is the binding constraint - you cannot push an arbitrary tarball; everything must be a signed source package (.dsc + orig.tar.gz + debian.tar.gz), so a 4 GB blob becomes one 4 GB .orig.tar.gz (allowed, but must be a valid Debian source package). retention: indefinite - 'A published package remains available until ..

egress.terms: Free: 'Data transfer | No fixed cap; unusual volumes may trigger contact from Launchpad.' Served from ppa.launchpadcontent.net with no billing.

tooling: `dput`/`dput-ng` (rsync+ftp upload to ppa.launchpad.net), `apt`/`deb-src` for consumption, Launchpad REST API + `launchpadlib`. No rclone backend.
chaining: Users and teams can create multiple Personal Package Archives with 8 GiB capacity each. Aggregating capacity scales across distinct PPA repositories and signing keys.
limits_note: per-object-cap: 'Uploadable artefacts | Source packages only; pre-built binary uploads are rejected' and 'Package formats | .deb only'. This is the binding constraint - you cannot push an arbitrary tarball; everything must be a signed source package (.dsc + orig.tar.gz + debian.tar.gz), so a 4 GB blob becomes one 4 GB .orig.tar.gz (allowed, but must be a valid Debian source package). retention: indefinite - 'A published package remains available until ... the owner removes it, or a later upload supersedes it.' request-rate: not documented; download is plain HTTP. Measured single-stream throughput on a real PPA .deb was only ~70 KB/s.

identity_cost.detail: no identity_cost field and no identity statement in the source record; defaulted to email and flagged, not evidence

reliability_note: The read path works and supports ranges (verified 206 on a 1 MB range of a real .deb) but single-connection speed was poor (~70,666 B/s over 15 s). Batch/sharded fetch needed. Upload requires GPG-signed source packages - no arbitrary blob PUT. help.launchpad.net and blog.launchpad.net returned 503 to the reader all session (used archive captures instead), so the live help site is unreliable to fetch programmatically.
